articles.title: ‘He still has a lot to prove’: Waqar Younis makes bold claim on Jasprit Bumrah
articles.summary: Former Pakistan captain Waqar Younis has hailed Jasprit Bumrah as the standout bowler in modern-day white-ball cricket but believes the Indian fast bowler
articles.body: Former Pakistan captain Waqar Younis has hailed Jasprit Bumrah as the standout bowler in modern-day white-ball cricket but believes the Indian fast bowler still has more to establish in the Test format.Despite Bumrah's impressive record of 234 wickets in 52 Tests at an average of 19.7 and a strike rate of 42.8, Waqar feels the pacer has not played enough red-ball cricket to be placed ahead of other leading fast bowlers.“There’s no modern-day bowler of the same calibre as Bumrah with the white ball. Leave out Test cricket. He still has a lot to prove in Tests; he hasn’t played as much. There are plenty of others, like Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood. You can’t ignore some of the English bowlers either. But when you talk about T20 and one-day cricket, I feel that in terms of impact, Bumrah always delivers in crunch scenarios. And that’s what matters,” Waqar said on the Shubhankar Mishra podcast.Waqar's assessment comes despite Bumrah's significant achievements in the longest format. The India pacer became the fastest Indian fast bowler to reach 50 Test wickets in 2018, accomplishing the milestone in his 11th match. He went on to claim his 100th Test wicket in his 24th appearance.Bumrah also became only the third Indian bowler to take a Test hat-trick in 2019. His performances in 2024 earned him the ICC Men's Test Cricketer of the Year award, while he finished the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy with 32 wickets in five Tests, a record haul for the series.The right-arm pacer has also been highly effective in England, taking 51 wickets in 11 Tests.One possible reason behind Waqar's assessment is Bumrah's limited availability in Test cricket compared with Australian quicks Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood. Injuries and workload management have affected his participation, and he is yet to play a Test for India this year.Bumrah is expected to return for India's two-match Test series in New Zealand next month, with a place in the World Test Championship final at stake.Waqar recalls Bumrah's match-winning spell against PakistanWhile questioning Bumrah's standing in Tests, Waqar was unequivocal about the Indian pacer's influence in ODIs and T20Is. He particularly remembered Bumrah's decisive contribution in India's six-run victory over Pakistan at the 2024 T20 World Cup in New York.Pakistan appeared firmly in control at 80/3 after 14 overs, needing only 40 runs from the final six overs to chase India's target of 120. Bumrah dismissed Mohammad Rizwan, triggering a collapse that helped India defend the modest total.Waqar believes that spell demonstrated why Bumrah is such a valuable asset in high-pressure situations, particularly when a captain needs a breakthrough.“Whenever an India captain is in trouble, he always gives the ball to Bumrah. Pakistan had no business losing in New York. The required rate was well under control. That over in which Bumrah dismissed Rizwan proved to be the difference. Impact players are the key players. A top player can motivate others who too feel that we have to match him,” said Waqar, who took 373 wickets in Test cricket for Pakistan.For Waqar, Bumrah's greatest strength in white-ball cricket is his ability to deliver when the stakes are highest, making him a decisive figure in crucial moments.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: South Africa vs Australia, third Test: Josh Inglis hits second Test century as Temba Bavuma's side take narrow lead
articles.summary: Josh Inglis starred with his second hundred in Test cricket as Australia seized momentum by stumps on day three of the third Test; South Africa ended the day 40 runs ahead but four second-innings wickets down; watch day four live on Friday from 8am on Sky Sports Cricket
articles.body:
After South Africa were bowled out for 329 on day one, Pat Cummins' side took a 100-run lead, before being bowled out for 429 after lunch.

Alex Carey and Inglis pushed the visitors in front with a fifth-wicket stand of 185, as Inglis advanced to his century off 132 deliveries.

South Africa fought back to match Australia's lead but found themselves on the back foot later in the afternoon, with Aiden Markram (1), Marques Ackerman (62) and David Bedingham (11) all being removed for 132 inside 28.2 overs.

Skipper Temba Bavuma arrived at the crease and brilliantly ground down the Australian pace attack to make 35 runs off 115 deliveries off a strike rate of 30.43, before Nathan Lyon struck a huge body blow.

Lyon jagged a beautiful off-spinner around Bavuma's bat and into his middle stump to remove the South African captain just five minutes before the close of play, with the hosts 140-4 at stumps and needing a big morning on Friday to advance their lead on day four.

The hosts' hopes of piling on a big lead were confronted by Mitchell Starc, who came firing out of the blocks in South Africa's second innings to bring his match haul up to eight wickets.

Markram first clumsily struck Starc up to Travis Head at mid-off in the third over before Josh Hazlewood's shorter delivery saw Bedingham pull the ball out to Lyon standing at deep square leg.

Ackerman and Bavuma combined brilliantly, with the former advancing to 62 off 80 deliveries. But just as he built momentum, Starc's bouncer struck his gloves before carrying to Cameron Green in the slips.

Matthew Breetzke (19) and Ryan Rickelton (8) will return to the crease on Friday.

Inglis, who hit 11 fours and two sixes, began the day needing 10 runs to reach his milestone, but his time at the crease on Thursday was short-lived, with Simon Harmer forcing him to edge behind to Rickelton for 102 for 135.

Harmer was the pick of the South African bowlers, also snaring Carey for 80, adding to his pair of wickets on day two to finish with figures of four for 104.

Kagiso Rabada trapped Cummins for no runs next, before Starc was caught behind by Rickelton off a Gerald Coetzee delivery for 11.

Harmer found himself in the centre of the action again after lunch, taking a brilliant catch in the slips to remove Nathan Lyon for one off a Wiaan Mulder delivery.

articles.title: Bhuvneshwar Kumar struggles on India comeback, Ashwin points out major concerns: 'I thought his pace was down'
articles.summary: Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return to India’s T20I setup has not gone according to plan, with former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin delivering a blunt
articles.body: Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return to India’s T20I setup has not gone according to plan, with former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin delivering a blunt assessment of the veteran pacer’s performance in the third T20I against New Zealand.Bhuvneshwar, who returned to the national side after nearly four years, has struggled to make an impact in the ongoing five-match series. The 36-year-old has conceded 139 runs in 12 overs across his first three outings, picking up just one wicket at an economy rate of 11.58.His struggles continued in the third T20I, where he finished with figures of 0/40 in four overs as New Zealand posted 199/5. India chased down the target to take a 3-0 lead in the series.‘A very big miss’: Ashwin questions Bhuvneshwar’s performanceSpeaking on SonyLIV after the match, Ashwin described Bhuvneshwar’s latest outing as a “miss”, pointing to a noticeable drop in pace and the absence of his trademark swing.“Bhuvneshwar Kumar in his third match is a miss for me. Look, anybody can go for runs. I would actually take the previous two games of Bhuvi. I thought he bowled really well upfront. He swung the ball and bowled the third over inside the Powerplay in the previous game,” Ashwin said.Ashwin acknowledged that conceding runs is part of a bowler’s game but felt Bhuvneshwar looked short of his best during the third T20I.“So, it's very understandable to have one bad over in the back half, but in this game, I thought his pace was down. The swing was missing. Just didn't look like he was running up to the crease as well as he could. Looked a bit off, and I think it's been a very big miss,” he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s numbers in the New Zealand T20I seriesThe numbers underline the challenges faced by the experienced seamer since his return. Bhuvneshwar conceded 49 runs without taking a wicket in the opening T20I, followed by 50 runs and one wicket in the second match. He then went wicketless again in the third game, giving away 40 runs.His expensive start has raised questions over his effectiveness in the side, particularly with India having already taken an unassailable 3-0 lead in the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sri Lanka vs England: Ben Duckett, Liam Dawson deliver ODI career bests for Harry Brook's side in consolation 55-run win
articles.summary: Sri Lanka were bowled out for 331 in reply to England's 386-5 in Lahore; Liam Dawson (4-49) impresses for Harry Brook's side, who saw Ben Duckett score 167 in their first win of the ODI tri-series; Sri Lanka play Pakistan in Saturday's final, live on Sky Sports Cricket (8am first ball)
articles.body:
England's hopes of reaching Saturday's final in Pakistan were already over after three consecutive group stage defeats, but Harry Brook's side successfully defended a commanding target of 387 and claimed a consolation win.

Duckett fired 167 from just 132 deliveries and put on big partnerships with Tom Banton (74) and Brook (44), as England scored 386-5 after losing the toss and batting first.

Pavan Rathnayake led the reply with 118 from 77 deliveries and Kusal Mendis (89) also impressed, with Sri Lanka threatening to pull off another famous chase - like they managed against England last week - when they passed 300 with five wickets still in hand.

Liam Dawson (4-49) made the Rathnayake breakthrough and Sonny Baker (2-75) also took key wickets, while Henry Crocombe, Joe Root and Sam Curran claimed one each, as Sri Lanka were dismissed for 331 after 45.1 overs.

How England ended ODI tri-series with victory

England almost made a nightmare start when Banton edged Asitha Fernando's opening ball of the innings just short of slip, although quickly pushed forward to post 62-0 from the powerplay.

Duckett made a 46-ball half-century and Banton reached his from 49 balls - a fifth in seven innings, with the pair's 163-run stand ended when Banton chopped an inside edge off Dasun Shanaka (1-49) onto his own stumps.

England surpassing the 429 they posted against Sri Lanka last week looked a possibility when they accelerated after the second drinks break, with Brook (44) adding a 107 partnership with Duckett before being caught and bowled attempting to scoop Asitha (2-63).

Duckett's brilliant innings - including 24 fours - ended when he picked out Asitha at short leg as he attempted to scoop a Malinga full toss, with England electing to push Joe Root down the order to focus on power hitting over the closing overs.

Will Jacks (30 off 21) was bowled by Asitha and Jordan Cox thrashed 43 off 27 balls, before being caught off Dilshan Madushanka's final ball of the innings, while Sam Curran finished unbeaten on 21 off 12 deliveries as England set another commanding target.

Baker - replacing Jamie Overton in England's only change - dropped Avishka on five when attempt a tough diving catch off Atkinson, although made a breakthrough in the following over when he bowled Kamindu Mendis (four).

Avishka (48) was caught on the boundary off Dawson to end an 84-run stand with Kusal, who recovered from his bat snapping early in his innings to fire 13 boundaries - including five sixes - to leave Sri Lanka on target at the halfway stage of their chase.

Kusal was left furious at himself after seeing his 71-ball innings ended by Root (1-35), with a faint touch on a sweep caught behind by Cox, before a successful review saw Dawson trap Shanaka lbw for four and swing momentum temporarily move back England's way.

Baker removed Janith Liyanage (27 off 17) after his quickfire stand with Rathnayake, who brought up his century - a second in as many matches against England - off 70 balls and lifted Sri Lanka past 300 with Sahan Arachchige.

Crocombe saw Arachchige (30) caught by Brook in the deep and Wellalage (one) was run out in calamitous fashion, where he sacrificed himself at the striker's end to avoid Rathnayake being dismissed.

Rathnayake top-edged Dawson to short fine leg to all-but end Sri Lanka hopes, with Asitha (one) and Malinga (one) then out cheaply, as England took the last three wickets in six deliveries to complete their win with 29 balls to spare.

Brook praises 'exceptional' England effort in victory

"You just want to score runs and put us in a good position. To get over the line is great - we've played some great cricket, we just haven't been getting the right side of the results.

"The pitches are really good to bat on here - you've seen the amount of runs in the series. My previous tours to Pakistan have probably helped, but it's a great place to bat. Tom Banton has been great coming in at the top of the order and taken a lot of pressure off me - he scores freely."

England captain Harry Brook, speaking at the presentation:

"We've batted really well throughout the series, apart from that first game. We've put on a fairly dominant performance with the bat and then I think, the way we finished the game off tonight, we've learned a lot from the game when Sri Lanka chased 430 - that's really good to see.

"I wasn't getting nervous [when Sri Lanka chased] - we had a clear plan and a lot of clarity with the bowlers. The ball was getting softer and I think that played a little bit of a factor. The lads have learned a hell of a lot and to finish off the game like we did there was an exceptional effort.

"We haven't had the series we'd have wanted coming here, we'd have liked to be in the final on Saturday, but unfortunately we're not. I think the lads are taking a lot of confidence from this series, albeit on the wrong side. All in all, despite the losses, it's been a good series."

England will play a 50-over warm-up game against Western Australia XI on November 7, played at the WACA ground in Perth, before a three-match ODI series and five-match T20 series against Australia.

The ODI series starts in Perth on November 13 before further fixtures in Adelaide (November 15) and Hobart (November 18), before the T20 action gets under way at the MCG in Melbourne on November 21.

articles.title: Ben Duckett and Liam Dawson impress as England beat Sri Lanka to end tri-series
articles.summary: Ben Duckett hits 167 and Liam Dawson takes four wickets as England end the tri-series with victory over Sri Lanka.
articles.body:
One-day international tri-series, Lahore

England 386-5 (50 overs): Duckett 167 (132); Asitha 2-63

Sri Lanka 331 (45.1 overs): Rathnayake 118 (77); Dawson 4-49

Ben Duckett's sublime century and four wickets for Liam Dawson earned England a consolation win over Sri Lanka in their final match of the tri-series.

Duckett struck a majestic 167 from 132 balls as England racked up 386-5 in Lahore, which set up a tantalising chase after Sri Lanka's astonishing pursuit of 430 in their previous encounter a week ago.

In another high-scoring match with very little contest between bat and ball, the chase followed a similar trajectory, as Sri Lanka kept themselves within touching distance of the run-rate throughout and needed 87 off the final 10 overs.

But England's bowlers held their nerve on this occasion, closing out a 55-run win as the brilliant Pavan Rathnayake's 118 off just 77 balls was in vain for Sri Lanka.

Rathnayake, who made 130 in last week's carnage, set the platform alongside Kusal Mendis' 89 but Sri Lanka lost their last five wickets for just 16 runs, with Dawson claiming the key scalp of Rathnayake in the 45th over as they were all out for 331.

It meant Duckett's second consecutive century eclipsed Rathnayake's effort, as England's opener capitalised on a batting-friendly surface and a tiring Sri Lanka attack.

The opening partnership between Duckett and Tom Banton impressed again as the pair added 163 together before the latter frustratingly dragged on to his stumps for a fine 74.

Duckett kicked on to his highest ODI score and though England fell short of the 400 mark, contributions of 44 from Harry Brook, 30 from Will Jacks and a quickfire 43 off 27 from Jordan Cox ensured they still posted a commanding total.

Such is the power of England's middle order that Root was not required to bat.

It was far from ideal for Sri Lanka's bowlers to toil in the heat as they face Pakistan in the tri-series final on Sunday, while England travel to Australia for three ODIs and five T20s in November.

How good is England’s ODI side a year out from the World Cup?

Duckett delights as Banton takes his chance

While Duckett's 105 against Pakistan held a poor England innings together, here he was ruthless.

With very little swing or seam movement on offer, Duckett was able to back himself to flay anything wide of the off stump and timed the ball exquisitely off his pads when Sri Lanka were forced to bowl straighter.

They attempted to test with the short ball, too, but he was particularly prolific against it as the seamers lacked the pace to really trouble him.

It was also an impressive display of fitness from a player who has spoken about how hard he has worked at that part of his game, eventually falling in the 42nd over from a miscued ramp as the fatigue appeared to take its toll.

Duckett seems to relish opening with Banton: the pair have stands of 143, 6, 91, 74, 4 and 163 in their past six outings together. That, and Banton's form, has given England's selectors an intriguing conundrum for when Jacob Bethell returns from injury in Australia.

Bethell previously occupied the opening slot alongside Duckett but Banton, with five scores of fifty plus in his past six knocks, looks likely to have nailed down his place on this tour, despite some frustration that he could not kick on to three figures when conditions were so favourable.

"You want options, and guys to push their case when they get their opportunities," England coach Brendon McCullum told Sky Sports after the game.

"They're good problems for us to have. We will learn more about that in Australia, but we will always do what's right for the team depending on conditions and the opposition."

Bethell's versatility could potentially see him find a place in the middle order, but it is a promising indication of England's impressive white-ball depth that it is unclear who he could replace from Root, Brook and Jacks, with Jordan Cox needed as keeper in Jos Buttler's injury absence.

Careless dismissals give Australia route to series win

Dawson takes four as England complete 55-run win over Sri Lanka - as it happened

The tri-series has exposed some of England's inexperienced bowling, particularly in the middle overs, and with Jamie Overton missing out to Sonny Baker it looked like England were going to rue the omission of leg-spinner Adil Rashid again.

The experienced Dawson saved their blushes though, starting with the crucial wicket of opener Avishka Fernando, who picked out Jacks on the boundary to break a second-wicket stand of 82. Dawson then pinned the explosive Dasun Shanaka lbw for four after Root surprisingly had Mendis caught down the leg side.

Rathnayake raced to a 70-ball century to keep Sri Lanka in contention, and a fifth-wicket stand of 72 off just 38 balls with the explosive Janith Liyanage had England twitching before the latter fell to Baker for 27 off 17.

Dawson then added Rathnayake and Asitha Fernando to his tally when the run-rate spiralled in the closing stages, while Sam Curran and Baker also executed well at the death to recover from their expensive starts early in the innings.

The question surrounding England's second spinner remains, however, as part-timers Jacks and Root conceded 71 off seven combined overs which could have given Brook a headache had Sri Lanka's run chase progressed deeper.

"Leg-spin hasn't played too much of a role and we want to be a team who can adapt to different conditions and be quite malleable with our selections," McCullum added.

"Liam Dawson is an experienced and highly competitive player who's put his hand up here and unfortunately for Rash here, the conditions probably haven't really favoured him."

articles.title: South Africa vs Australia: Careless dismissals give tourists route to series win
articles.summary: Australia take a step towards victory over South Africa in Cape Town, with the help of careless batting from Proteas' top order.
articles.body:
Third Test, Cape Town (day three of five)

South Africa 329 & 140-4: Ackerman 62; Starc 2-29

Batters carelessly gifting wickets to Australia... we have been here before.

This time it was not England helping their opponents, although they will have taken note with a tour of South Africa to come this winter.

South Africa's attempt to fight back in the decisive third Test against Australia was hurt by two poor strokes on day three.

Having taken the last six Australian wickets for 99 runs in the morning despite Josh Inglis' second Test century, the Proteas began their second innings facing a deficit of exactly 100.

They needed runs from their experienced opener and number three. Neither Aiden Markram nor David Bedingham could deliver.

By the end, even captain Temba Bavuma had been tempted into a wild swipe to fall for 35. South Africa were 140-4, just 40 runs ahead, at the close.

In isolation, Markram's drive off Mitchell Starc straight into the hands of mid-off for one appeared the most egregious.

The ball was the fullest of the six balls Markram faced but not there for him to play his trademark shot. Fielder Travis Head did not have to move.

Worse, though, was the dismissal of Bedingham, who showed he had not learned from the first innings.

Then, the right-hander top-edged a pull to Josh Hazlewood off the bowling of Starc. This time he repeated the shot, with Hazlewood the wicket-taking bowler.

"That is just absolutely soft from David Bedingham," said former South Africa bowler Vernon Philander.

"He knew they were going to target him in that zone. For the second time in the Test, he has fallen to the same ploy."

Given the prized position in South Africa's batting order on the back of strong domestic form for Durham in the County Championship and twin hundreds for Western Province in September, this score of 11 followed contributions of 49, 46 and 50 in his other four innings.

He has got in but has not made a match-winning contribution.

Batting in the key position of first drop, some would say that is more infuriating than not getting in at all.

His dismissal, again like in the first innings, came shortly after being hit by a bouncer, with Starc clattering one into his chest on this occasion.

When, after starting with two balls on a good length, Hazlewood went short again, Bedingham's eyes lit up.

Ollie Robinson, Jofra Archer and co should have been taking note. It was the fifth time he has been dismissed pulling in his 18 Tests.

On average he gets out playing that shot once every 13 deliveries.

"He never looks in the right position to play the pull or hook shot," former South Africa captain Graeme Smith said. "He is always off balance. He is never in a strong position.

"You think about best pullers in the game they have a strong base. He is pirouetting on one leg.

"[South Africa great] Hashim Amla just put the pull shot away for a phase.

"That is what a player like Bedingham needs to think about."

Duckett and Dawson deliver in England's consolation win

Bavuma, in contrast, dug in for 115 balls in which he hit only one boundary.

As he had in his 179 in the second-Test win in Gqeberha which set up this grand Cape Town finale, he showed his side the way in a partnership lasting 17.3 overs with Matthew Breetzke after opener Marques Ackerman had briskly made 65 before being bounced out by Starc.

But with four minutes to go in the day, Australia captain Pat Cummins tweaked his field for spinner Nathan Lyon.

Bavuma had pushed and driven outside off stump to that point but, with a silly point now in place, he was dragged from his crease and tried to force through mid-wicket.

Australia's celebrations suggested they believe that was the crucial wicket.

The vicious turn Lyon found means any chase over 200 would not be straightforward for Australia. South Africa's spinner Simon Harmer dismissed Inglis and Alex Carey (80) earlier in the day on his way to figures of 4-104.

The Proteas have Breetzke and Ryan Rickelton at the crease - and Test triple-centurion Wiaan Mulder to come, before in-form all-rounder Marco Jansen and the tail.

This still appears a tall order, however.

As on day one and two, Australia have held firm and their opponents faltered. England know that feeling too.

articles.title: Pakistan rights activist Imaan Mazari and husband jailed for 10 years
articles.summary: Couple say they are ‘prisoners of conscience’ being made an example of by Pakistan’s military-backed authorities.
articles.body:
An antiterrorism court in Pakistan has sentenced prominent human rights lawyers Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, ⁠⁠to 10 years in prison on terrorism-related charges.

Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra announced the verdict on Thursday, following their trial inside Adiala prison in the garrison city of Rawalpindi.

The couple were found guilty of putting “the security of [the England and Wales Cricket] team at risk”, the judge wrote, adding that it “clearly shows the intentions and objective of the accused to create a sense of terror”, according to a copy of the court judgement obtained by the AFP news agency.

At the same time, the ruling conceded that the security breach was “a very common nature ordinary type of incident apparently of removal of a barrier”.

The case relates to an October 2024 incident in which the couple removed road barriers in the capital, Islamabad, along a route designated for the touring England cricket team.

The couple were indicted on October 7, accused of obstructing police and inciting public interest, and pleaded not guilty.

In statements seen by the Reuters news agency, the couple denied the charges, while calling themselves “prisoners of conscience”, adding that ⁠⁠they were being targeted for their human rights work.

In their defence document, the couple had earlier said they were “being made an example to further cement the chilling effect against those who stand (or want to stand) against tyranny, oppression and injustice”.

Shireen Mazari, who is Imaan Mazari’s mother and served as Pakistan’s human rights minister under incarcerated former Prime Minister Imran Khan, said it was a “sham trial without any due process”.

Mazari told the Reuters news agency the couple “were not permitted to defend themselves through their own lawyer, and were not provided with key legal ⁠⁠documents”, adding that the defence would file a petition against the verdict in the Supreme Court.

Amnesty International called the convictions “an indictment of Pakistan’s justice system.”

“It was a test of the judiciary’s ability to uphold the principles of justice and the right to fair trial. It has failed that test miserably,” said Amnesty’s Yasmine Ahmend.

“It is clear that these ‘anti-terrorism’ charges are being used to punish Imaan and Hadi for their human rights advocacy,” she added.

Mazari and Chattha have been in custody since January 23, in a separate case over their social media posts.

A lower court sentenced ‌‌them each to 17 years the next day under Pakistan’s Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, which critics have said is designed to quash antigovernment dissent online.

Although the Supreme Court later suspended those sentences, police re-arrested ‌‌the couple the same day in the security breach case.

“Imaan and Hadi’s re-arrest dispels any pretence that the charges against them are anything other than a politically motivated attempt to punish them for their human rights work”, said Babu Ram Pant, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director for South Asia, adding that the case demonstrates once again the authorities’ willingness to weaponise the legal system against critical voices.

Pakistan’s ⁠⁠law minister, Azam Nazeer Tarar, has repeatedly said the country’s judiciary is independent.

articles.title: England head coach Brendon McCullum hails captain Harry Brook after tourists end ODI tri-series with consolation win
articles.summary: England boss Brendon McCullum talks Harry Brook's leadership, Adil Rashid's omission and the lessons learned as tourists earn victory at last in ODI tri-series; after missing out on the final, McCullum's men now focused on white-ball tour of Australia in November (three ODIs, five T20s)
articles.body:
England lost their first three matches after a botched run chase against Pakistan was followed by failing to defend a total of 429 against Sri Lanka and then suffering another defeat to Pakistan as the hosts reached a target of 242 despite having been 154-9.

Brook's side looked in danger of a fourth loss from four when Pavan Rathnayake scored his second hundred against England in as many matches on Thursday but they eventually bowled Sri Lanka out for 331 as their opponents pursued a target of 387.

Speaking to Sky Sports Cricket , head coach McCullum said of Brook: "He's one of the best tactical captains I've ever come across.

"He's got such an astute brain. He wears his intelligence lightly externally but he's a very switched on man and cricketer.

"He has the respect of the entire dressing room. He leads and they follow him. He is interactive with his leadership. It's not just him on his own, he calls on other people.

"He will have learned a lot from getting thrust into a situation like this where the game is travelling at breakneck speed, and you're having to make decisions which can win or lose a game.

"Providing you have the ability to take stock post-game, assess the situation and come up with new ideas [you can improve].

"We saw that [against Sri Lanka]. We were probably behind the game when they were five down but Brooky was able to slow it down, make some plays and we were able to get the wickets we needed.

"He would have grown enormously. I can't talk highly enough of his captaincy, not just his tactics but also his leadership."

Left-arm spinner Liam Dawson picked up the key wicket of Rathnayake, caught sweeping to short fine leg, in the 45th over with Sri Lanka needing 58 runs from 35 balls.

The 36-year-old bagged figures of 4-49 on the day and claimed seven wickets in three games at an average of 21.42 in the competition after replacing leg-spinner Adil Rashid following England's opening defeat to Pakistan in Rawalpindi.

Rashid, 38, is England's second-highest ODI wicket-taker of all time, behind only James Anderson, and McCullum suggested the Yorkshireman dropping out of the side in the tri-series was solely down to conditions.

The New Zealander added: "We will always do what we think is right for the conditions and the opposition we are playing against

"Dawson has done well out here with left-am spin having a significant impact on this tournament whereas leg-spin hasn't had much of a role.

"We want to be a team that can adapt to different conditions, be malleable and have that flexibility.

"Dawson is a highly-competitive player who has put his hand up and on this occasion, the conditions probably went against Rash."

'We know we need to get better - but we will'

England's preparations for the 2027 50-over World Cup in South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe next take them to Australia in November with three ODIs followed by five T20 internationals.

Batter Jacob Bethell and fast bowler Jofra Archer will return after missing the tri-series in Pakistan due to a knee injury and rest respectively, but wicketkeeper-batter Jos Buttler remains sidelined while he recovers from hamstring surgery.

Bethell had been opening the batting with Ben Duckett in ODIs prior to his knee issue in the home summer, although may now face a battle to regain his spot immediately.

Tom Banton has struck one hundred, and four fifties, in seven innings since taking Bethell's place, while Duckett closed out the tri-series with successive centuries, including a career-best 167 from 132 balls.

McCullum says selection dilemmas are "good problems" to have as he reflected on what England have gleaned from their trip to the subcontinent.

"For us to be exposed at times but succeed at others - we have seen lot of guys step up and perform and others have great lessons learned from this trip," the head coach added.

"It is going to hold us in good stead moving forward. We know we had some missed opportunities in this series but we did some really good stuff.

"We bounced back in our final game, holding our nerve [with the ball] when the dewy conditions were against us. That was satisfying but we know we have a lot to learn.

"We want to be a team that challenges seriously for that World Cup and we know we need to get better - but we will. This experience has been very good for us, albeit it has been disappointing in terms of not making the final."

articles.title: Azmatullah Omarzai scripts history after walking in at 5/4, smashes T20I world record
articles.summary: Azmatullah Omarzai produced a stunning rescue act with the bat, smashing a record-breaking century to help Afghanistan recover from a disastrous start and
articles.body: Azmatullah Omarzai produced a stunning rescue act with the bat, smashing a record-breaking century to help Afghanistan recover from a disastrous start and post 221/7 against Zimbabwe in the second T20I at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium on Thursday.Walking in with Afghanistan reeling at 5/4, Omarzai launched a counter-attack that completely changed the course of the innings. He hammered 116 off just 50 balls, striking five fours and 12 sixes at an astonishing strike rate of 232.With the effort, Omarzai registered the highest individual score by a batter coming in at No. 6 or lower in T20Is involving Full Member nations. He went past the previous record of 89, scored by former Afghanistan captain Mohammad Nabi against Ireland in 2017.The record-breaking knock also put Omarzai ahead of Sam Billings (87 against West Indies in 2019), Cameron White (85 not out against Sri Lanka in 2010) and David Miller (85 not out against Pakistan in 2021) on the list.Afghanistan's innings had been in complete disarray after Zimbabwe's bowlers reduced them to 5/4. Several top-order batters departed cheaply, while Sediqullah Atal managed just 17 off 21 deliveries before falling in the ninth over.Omarzai found an ideal partner in Ijaz Ahmad Ahmadzai, and the duo launched a remarkable recovery. They added 142 runs off only 59 balls for the sixth wicket, with Ijaz contributing a blistering 52 off 27 deliveries, including five fours and three sixes.The partnership was finally broken when Ijaz fell with the score at 180. Omarzai continued his assault before being dismissed in the 19th over, having already produced one of the finest rescue acts in Afghanistan's T20I history.Captain Rashid Khan provided a spectacular finish, smashing an unbeaten 25 off just six balls, including four sixes. Mujeeb Ur Rahman remained not out on two as Afghanistan closed their innings at 221/7, scoring at 11.05 runs per over.Rashid also achieved a major milestone during the match, becoming the first bowler to claim 200 wickets in T20Is.Zimbabwe fall short despite Sikandar Raza's centuryZimbabwe were unable to overcome the imposing target despite a determined effort from captain Sikandar Raza, who scored his second T20I century.Raza fought till the end, but the visitors ultimately fell short, with Afghanistan's early batting collapse proving to be a distant memory after Omarzai's extraordinary intervention.Tafadzwa Tsiga offered valuable support on his debut, while the dismissal of Ryan Burl dealt another blow to Zimbabwe's hopes.The victory also extended Afghanistan's remarkable dominance in the rivalry, marking their eighth consecutive T20I series win against Zimbabwe. The visitors are yet to win a T20I series against Afghanistan.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'I was very happy': Smriti Mandhana reveals MS Dhoni's special WhatsApp message after World Cup win
articles.summary: Smriti Mandhana has revealed that former India captain MS Dhoni personally congratulated her after the Indian women's team lifted their maiden ODI World
articles.body: Smriti Mandhana has revealed that former India captain MS Dhoni personally congratulated her after the Indian women's team lifted their maiden ODI World Cup title in November 2025.Speaking at an event featuring Dhoni, Mandhana recalled receiving a WhatsApp message from the legendary cricketer following India's historic triumph. She admitted that the gesture made her particularly happy, knowing that Dhoni is not someone who uses his phone frequently.“He actually did send me a message after the World Cup win. I know he does not use his phone a lot. I was very happy that he used WhatsApp to congratulate all of us," Mandhana said.Host Harsha Bhogle then asked Mandhana whether she had saved Dhoni's number.“I did have his number," she replied.Dhoni, meanwhile, offered an interesting explanation for choosing Mandhana as the recipient of his message. He revealed that she was the only member of the Indian women's team whose contact number he had saved.“I did not know anyone else’s (number) from the team. I wanted the message to go through. We had just shot (a commercial) before that. I thought, ‘Let me send a message to Smriti’ and I mentioned, ‘Please wish everyone who is part of the team," Dhoni said.India created history on November 2, 2025, defeating South Africa by 52 runs in Navi Mumbai to win their first-ever Women's ODI World Cup. The triumph ended the team's long wait for an ICC title.Batting first in the final, India posted 298/7, with Shafali Verma leading the charge with 87 runs and Deepti Sharma contributing 58. Deepti then delivered with the ball, taking five wickets as South Africa were dismissed for 246 despite a century from Laura Wolvaardt.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Time for the victory lap: India aim to maintain unbeaten run in Auckland as New Zealand look to avoid whitewash
articles.summary: The series is settled. Now it's time for some fun.
articles.body: The series is settled. Now it's time for some fun. Team India, the Harlem Globetrotters of world cricket, have continued their march through New Zealand, arriving from humid home conditions just a day before the series began and making it 3-0 in style over the course of just a week, which teams would normally use to acclimatise to foreign conditions.After the stupendous feasts the batters enjoyed on the drop-in pitches in Christchurch and Wellington, the focus shifts to unique Eden Park in Auckland, a ground originally built with rugby in mind.The straight boundaries here are probably only a little longer than your backyard, while the longer square boundaries will test the power of India's hitmen. New Zealand's bowlers will need the motivation to bend their backs after watching India chase 199 in 13.2 overs on Tuesday.The Black Caps are already hampered by the absence of experienced pacers Matt Henry and Lockie Ferguson, both sidelined by injury, and the Indian batters should be licking their lips.Ravi Shastri said on air the other day that a question he gets asked often in New Zealand is: "Will that 15-year-old play?" Wellington fans got a glimpse of the young sensation as he smashed a 19-ball 45 in the third game, an innings that, remarkably, played second fiddle to Abhishek Sharma's 38-ball 113.Sooryavanshi's opportunity came because of Ishan Kishan's injury, but Indian spin legend R Ashwin feels that if the Jharkhand batter returns to the XI, Sanju Samson should reclaim his opening slot and Vaibhav should miss out.That's cold cricket analysis. The Indian diaspora that will troop to Eden Park on Friday evening will surely hope to enjoy another Vaibhav feast, perhaps this time in a lead role. His ability to generate incredible power against the short ball, along with his straight-hitting, should be enough for the team management to let the fun continue.If Gautam Gambhir and Co. are serious about testing the temperament and skill of the Indian pace attack, Eden Park should be an ideal venue. If the pitch remains a belter, as it often is in T20Is in New Zealand, the Indian quicks' ability to hit a hard length will be tested.Landing yorkers, both wide and at the stumps, is one of this attack's strengths. But at Eden Park, they have to be inch-perfect: a slight error in length can turn a delivery into a gift that sails into the stands.Ahead of practice on Thursday, India vice-captain Tilak Varma said the team was impressed by how Prince Yadav and the other bowlers had landed their yorkers."They have been brilliant at the back end, especially Prince with the yorkers. But Eden Park is new for many of us, and we'll have to work out the right length once we understand the pitch," said Varma, who has been phenomenal with his finishing in the series.Paceman Mayank Yadav was left out of the last two games after returning figures of 1/49 in the first. Bhuvneshwar Kumar, on his return, has conceded 49, 50 and 40 runs in the three games he has played, taking one wicket.Mayank's burst of pace could come in handy. With the series already won, it would not be a bad time for the team management to look to the future.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Tanush Kotian takes career-best 8-81 as Mumbai secure third bonus point win
articles.summary: Mumbai: Off-spinner Tanush Kotian produced a career-best 8-81 and an impressive match haul of 11-151 as Mumbai crushed Haryana by 10 wickets on the fourth
articles.body: Mumbai: Off-spinner Tanush Kotian produced a career-best 8-81 and an impressive match haul of 11-151 as Mumbai crushed Haryana by 10 wickets on the fourth and final day of their Ranji Trophy Elite Group D clash at the MCA ground.The win gave Mumbai their third successive bonus-point victory of the season, marking their best start in a long time. They now have 21 points from three matches - the most among all teams in the Ranji Trophy - and sit atop their group, firmly placed on the road to the knockouts.Mumbai will next take on Railways at the Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India from November 2-5.The match will remain special for Kotian, who was playing his 50th first-class game. He marked the occasion with his first 10-wicket match haul and his fourth five-wicket haul.Chasing a modest target of 97, Mumbai openers Angkrish Raghuvanshi and Divyaansh Saxena completed the job in just 10.4 overs. Raghuvanshi, riding high after scoring his maiden first-class century in the first innings, smashed an unbeaten 67 off 39 balls. Saxena, who had struggled in his previous two innings, made a confidence-boosting 30 not out off 25 balls.The final day, however, was not entirely straightforward for Mumbai. Haryana's eighth-wicket pair of Samant Jakhar and Anuj Thakral made the hosts toil on a slow surface, adding 81 runs over nearly two hours.Kotian eventually broke the stand by bowling Jakhar. Haryana, who had resumed on 73-2, still 87 runs behind after following on, were bowled out for 256 in the second session.Reflecting on Mumbai's strong start to the season, Kotian said, "As a team, we've worked well. It's very difficult to get a third victory with a bonus point. Everyone is backing each other and giving confidence. We're trying to contribute together. If the team goal is going well, we want to keep moving forward like this."Brief scores: Mumbai 430 & 97-0 (Raghuvanshi 67*). Haryana 270 & (following-on) 256 (Kotian 8-81) Mumbai won by 10 wickets. Points: Mumbai 7, Haryana 0.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IPL 2027: Amidst winds of change, Rohit Sharma is the glue Mumbai Indians need right now
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Kieron Pollard's elevation as the new head coach and the exits of Mahela Jayawardene, Lasith Malinga, Paras Mhambrey and Carl Hopkinson from
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Kieron Pollard's elevation as the new head coach and the exits of Mahela Jayawardene, Lasith Malinga, Paras Mhambrey and Carl Hopkinson from the Mumbai Indians (MI) setup have already pressed the reset button in the camp. Appointments for the fielding coach and assistant coach are still pending, but the winds of change have well and truly arrived as the five-time Indian Premier League (IPL) winners look to return to their glory days.The biggest, and most crucial, piece in the puzzle, however, remains captaincy.Should they go back to Rohit Sharma? The man who led them to five titles and understands the setup better than any other player? Or should they adopt a forward-looking approach with someone like Tilak Varma? What about Jasprit Bumrah and Suryakumar Yadav?Rohit is 39 and isn't the best bet the franchise can make for the next cycle, but it's more about restoring normalcy, allowing Pollard to ease into his new role and possibly grooming the next leader in the final year of the ongoing cycle. After sweeping changes to the support staff, a sense of familiarity in the leadership group will only make the transition and preparation for future challenges smoother.Pollard and Rohit played together for several years at MI. The West Indian was part of the famous "engine room", also featuring Hardik and Krunal Pandya, that drove the franchise forward during their golden days and flourished when Rohit was at the helm.This is not to suggest that the two are the perfect recipe to restore order in that dressing room, but looking towards an inexperienced candidate at this stage will only complicate matters further. Tilak is taking giant strides in his cricketing career and is certainly the future leader of MI and Indian cricket. But right now, it's the delicate balancing act between need and want that could help the management find some answers.By no means should going back to Rohit come across as shutting the door on someone like Tilak. It's about keeping that door firmly secured until the stormy phase is well behind them and the management gains some sense of direction with the new personnel.The 2027 edition will be more about peaceful survival and getting things right as a group before the proper reset button is pressed ahead of the mega auction. Until then, even the biggest names in the setup, barring Hardik Pandya, whose potential trade is the talk of the town, will look to coexist. A sense of familiarity will help avoid the kind of drama that followed Pandya's high-profile trade in 2023.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Two of the greatest in history': Mike Hesson backs struggling Babar Azam, Fakhar Zaman with bold claim
articles.summary: Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson has backed senior batters Babar Azam and Fakhar Zaman to deliver in the ODI tri-series final against Sri Lanka on
articles.body: Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson has backed senior batters Babar Azam and Fakhar Zaman to deliver in the ODI tri-series final against Sri Lanka on Saturday, describing the duo as two of the greatest players in the country's cricket history.Hesson believes the big occasion could bring the best out of the experienced pair, who have struggled to make an impact with the bat during the tournament.“You are talking about two of the greatest players in Pakistan’s history in the top three. I expect big players to stand up in big games," Hesson told the Pakistan Cricket Board ahead of the final at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium.However, their recent numbers have raised questions over their current form. Babar has registered scores of 45, 34, 10 and 29, while Fakhar's returns read 16, 0, 10 and 5.Despite their lack of substantial contributions, Pakistan have managed to reach the final with three successive victories. They defeated Sri Lanka by 37 runs and England by 87 runs before edging past Sri Lanka by one wicket in a thrilling encounter, where Shadab Khan's unbeaten century proved decisive.Hesson said the team's ability to win games without significant contributions from some of its established batters was an encouraging sign. He also backed them to produce a match-winning performance when it matters most.“The fact that we have been able to achieve the wins that we have without the top order performing as well as we know they are capable of is a good sign," he said. “A couple of our key players are searching for that match-winning performance, and there’s no better place to do it than in a final."Pakistan's campaign has not been without setbacks. They suffered an eight-wicket defeat to Sri Lanka in their final league fixture, but Hesson remained satisfied with the team's overall progress.He acknowledged that Pakistan had played some good cricket without putting together a complete performance and hoped they would produce their best effort in the title clash.“It’s been a pretty good couple of weeks. We have played some decent cricket without being perfect. To get three wins in a row without contributions from a few of our key players is a good sign," he said.“I still don’t think we have played our best game yet. Hopefully, we are saving that for the final."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Australia tighten grip on Day 3 as Nathan Lyon removes Temba Bavuma in dramatic final moments
articles.summary: Nathan Lyon struck a crucial blow just before the close of play, dismissing South Africa captain Temba Bavuma to strengthen Australia's position in the
articles.body: Nathan Lyon struck a crucial blow just before the close of play, dismissing South Africa captain Temba Bavuma to strengthen Australia's position in the series-deciding third Test at Newlands on Thursday.South Africa ended day three at 140/4 in their second innings, but with a deficit of 100 runs overturned, they effectively had a lead of just 40 with six wickets remaining. Matthew Breetzke was unbeaten on 19, while Ryan Rickelton was on eight.Bavuma's departure came with only five minutes left in the day's play. The South African captain, who had battled for 115 balls to score 35, attempted to work Lyon towards the leg side but missed the delivery, which went through the gap between bat and pad to hit the stumps.It was the seventh time Lyon had dismissed Bavuma, including twice in the ongoing Test.Australia had earlier secured a 100-run first-innings advantage after being bowled out for 429. South Africa's reply began poorly, with Mitchell Starc removing Aiden Markram in the third over after the opener played a delivery straight to Travis Head at mid-off.David Bedingham became the next casualty shortly before tea, top-edging a pull against Josh Hazlewood to give Lyon a catch in the deep.South Africa's middle order briefly restored some stability through Bavuma and Marques Ackerman. Ackerman, who had scored 95 in the first innings, struck another half-century off 64 balls and appeared set for a substantial contribution before Starc dismissed him for 62. A short ball from the Australian pacer struck Ackerman's helmet grille before carrying to slip.Starc finished the day with figures of 2/29 and had taken eight wickets in the match. Australia will look to press home its advantage when play resumes, with the pitch expected to become increasingly difficult for batting.Inglis century headlines Australia's first inningsEarlier, Australia resumed day three at 330/4 but lost their remaining six wickets for 99 runs to finish on 429.Josh Inglis continued from his overnight score of 85 not out to register his second Test century, reaching the landmark off 132 deliveries. His innings included 11 fours and two sixes. Both his Test hundreds have come overseas, with his first being a 102 on debut in Sri Lanka last year.Inglis shared a 185-run fifth-wicket partnership with Alex Carey, who contributed 80 off 168 balls, hitting seven fours. Both batters were dismissed by Simon Harmer, who accounted for Inglis and Carey in the first hour.Harmer continued to trouble the Australian lower order, while Kagiso Rabada trapped Pat Cummins lbw for a six-ball duck. Gerald Coetzee then removed Starc, who was caught behind, leaving Australia at 411/8 at lunch.The visitors added only 29 runs after the break, with Cooper Connolly scoring 29 off 83 balls, including three fours.Harmer finished with figures of 4/104, while Marco Jansen claimed 3/60 as South Africa fought back after Australia's strong start.The three-match series is level at 1-1. Australia won the opening Test in Durban by 214 runs before South Africa bounced back with an innings-and-31-run victory in Gqeberha. The third Test will decide the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New variations, angles and better accuracy helping Kotian trouble batters
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Competing neck and neck with Madhya Pradesh's off-spinner Saransh Jain, Tanush Kotian is doing his best to stay in the race and in the radar of
articles.body: MUMBAI: Competing neck and neck with Madhya Pradesh's off-spinner Saransh Jain, Tanush Kotian is doing his best to stay in the race and in the radar of national selectors.On Thursday, the 28-year-old took a career-best eight for 81 in 34.3 overs in the second innings against Haryana. Having taken three for 70 in 30.5 overs in the first innings, Kotian finished with match figures of 11 for 151. His effort helped Mumbai register their third consecutive bonus-point win of the season, as they beat Haryana by 10 wickets at the MCA ground in BKC on the fourth and final day of their Ranji Trophy Elite Group D match.The match was a special one for Kotian as it was his 50th first-class appearance. He marked the occasion with his first 10-wicket haul in a match and his fourth five-wicket haul."I have had four years of progress and improvement in my bowling. I did a lot of tours, I was also with the India team. They all guided me a lot, like I was practising with (BCCI COE spin bowing coach) Sunil Joshi sir, Jatin (Paranjape) sir and Rajesh (Sanil) sir (childhood coach and mentor). A lot of people have guided me. I am trying to use that experience in my bowling," Kotian told reporters after the match.The off-spinner, who took three for 30 against Chandigarh in Mumbai's opening match of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season, said he had worked on his line and length, added new variations and tried different angles to trouble batters."I have improved a lot in line and length. I have brought in two-three variations which are helping me in deceiving and beating the batsman. I am trying to do that in every match and working on my accuracy as well. I have worked on different angles. Sometimes when I was bowling from over the wicket to the lefty, I was using angles and crease and it looked better as I was not allowing the batters to get set. It was helping me in creating pressure on the batsmen and doubts in their minds," he said.Explaining what worked for him against Haryana, Kotian said he focused on bowling in the right areas and asked for specific field placements to support his plans."I was looking to bowl in good areas and the field set-up that I needed, I was specifically asking for it and bowling accordingly. I was able to create opportunities and was in a good rhythm."Kotian also scored his 20th first-class half-century in Mumbai's first innings. He said he had been working on improving his batting while focusing on accuracy with the ball."I have worked on myself. In batting, I’m trying to contribute in the lower order and improve further but in bowling, I feel that I've worked a lot on my accuracy. I feel that's the key. I'm accurately bowling at the right place. I’m also talking to the ‘keeper as to how it is going and I am happy with that," he said.Kotian was also asked whether Saransh Jain's performances, including his 13 for 89 (7-40 & 6-49) against Bihar in the third round, had added to the competition for a place in the Indian team."No, it's not in my mind. Even though they selected Saran Jain, he's doing well. I'm doing well too. But my aim is to perform as well as I can in the Mumbai team, or whether it's Irani Cup or Duleep Trophy, wherever I go, in every match, I want to perform like that. In batting and bowling, the selectors will do their job and I want to do my job," he replied.'Morkel and Lyon guided me in Aus'Kotian is yet to make his Test debut for India, but he travelled with the team for the final two Tests of the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Australia. During the tour, he sought advice from India's bowling coach and former South Africa fast bowler Morne Morkel, as well as Australia's spin great Nathan Lyon."I worked with Morne Morkel. I also talked to Nathan Lyon who guided me. I was also with (Ravindra) Jadeja. (Like in Australia), the bounce is extra so how can I bowl more over-spin balls. Over there, Nathan Lyon guided me with the run-up and how to use the over-spin. Whatever I learnt there, I’m working on that and working with seam positions and variations so that is helping,” Kotian told reporters on Thursday.Asked whether he had made any technical changes to become more comfortable bowling around the wicket to right-handers, and whether he was thinking about a possible India call-up for the home Border-Gavaskar Trophy series in January-February 2027, Kotian said his focus was on improving his bowling across different angles.“As for the BGT, we’ll see. I’ve focused on being equally comfortable bowling ‘around the wicket’ and ‘over the wicket’ to both left-handers and right-handers. Since last year, I’ve worked on ensuring that no matter which angle the captain asks me to bowl from, I feel confident in executing it,” he said.Kotian bowled 65.3 overs across the two innings against Haryana, doing so in Mumbai's October heat and humidity. He said he had been waiting for an opportunity to bowl a long spell and wanted to give the captain confidence in his ability to do so."I was waiting for this opportunity. I was trying to bowl as much as I could. I think this is the first time that I've bowled this much in a match. I'm giving the captain the confidence that I can bowl this much and can get that many wickets as well. In the last four years, we were all getting wickets together and this time I got the opportunity. The ball was coming out from my hand well and I was getting the wickets from one end," the Vikhroli resident said.Of the eight wickets he took in the second innings, Kotian said he particularly enjoyed dismissing Haryana's well-set No. 8 batter Samant Jakhat, who scored 40. He bowled Jakhat to break an eighth-wicket partnership."There was a partnership for the eighth wicket, and to have got the ball through the bat and pad (for the breakthrough) was something crucial as the game opened up after that," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: IND vs NZ Live Score: India could use remaining matches to test bench strength Having secured the series with two matches still to play, India have an opportunity to experiment with their combinations. Any changes are unlikely to take away from the team's batting strength, but the remaining games could offer the management a chance to assess different options ahead of the ODI and Test assignments that follow the T20Is..IND vs NZ Live Score: Injury-hit New Zealand bowling attack faces uphill task New Zealand's preparations for the fourth T20I have been complicated by injuries to two experienced fast bowlers. Lockie Ferguson and Matt Henry have been ruled out of the remaining matches in the series, leaving the hosts with fewer options as they attempt to contain India's formidable batting line-up. Henry had already been expected to sit out the remaining T20Is with his workload in mind, while Ferguson was keen to play in front of the home crowd at Eden Park. Nathan Smith is expected to return after missing the third match with a low-grade niggle. His availability could provide some relief to a bowling unit that conceded 199 in just 13.2 overs..IND vs NZ Live Score: Mitchell Santner faces another stern test against India New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner has acknowledged that his team needs to find ways to stop India's top-order charge. The left-arm spinner remains one of the hosts' key weapons, having taken 30 wickets against India in T20Is, making him the joint-highest wicket-taker in this fixture. He is also the only New Zealand bowler with an economy rate below 10 in the ongoing series. However, India's aggressive approach has put the entire bowling unit under pressure. Santner will need support from the seamers and a clear tactical plan if New Zealand are to prevent another big chase and keep their hopes of avoiding a whitewash alive..IND vs NZ Live Score: Abhishek Sharma and Sooryavanshi lead India's batting charge India's batting line-up has been firing on all cylinders, with Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi making a particularly strong impression in the third T20I. The pair helped India chase 199 in just 13.2 overs in Wellington, leaving New Zealand's bowling attack with little room to recover. Their Powerplay aggression has been a major feature of the series, with India averaging 85 runs in the first six overs. The challenge for New Zealand will be to find early breakthroughs and prevent the Indian openers from dictating terms once again. Eden Park's short straight boundaries could make that task even tougher..IND vs NZ Live Score: Eden Park could provide another batting bonanza The fourth T20I moves to Eden Park, a venue where the boundary dimensions could make life difficult for the bowlers. The straight boundaries are particularly short, while the square boundaries are comparatively bigger. That contrast will require New Zealand's bowlers to be precise with their lengths and make smart use of their field placements. India have already shown how quickly they can take a game away from the opposition, and their power-packed top order will fancy the conditions. A successful T20I chase of 245 has previously been recorded at the venue, although the most recent T20I here in March was dominated by bowlers..IND vs NZ Live Score: India look to extend dominance as New Zealand search for answers India head into the fourth T20I with the series already in their pocket, but the defending T20 World Cup champions will have little reason to ease off. Three matches have produced three successful chases, and their latest performance in Wellington was a statement of intent. India chased down 199 in just 13.2 overs, with Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi leading the assault. New Zealand have struggled to contain the visitors' aggressive batting approach and must find a way to disrupt their rhythm. With two matches remaining, the hosts will be desperate to avoid a series whitewash.

MI have promoted him from batting coach to head coach, which gives the former West Indies all-rounder a new leadership role at the five-time IPL champions.

Pollard enjoyed a long and successful stint as a player with MI, and he stayed with the team in a coaching capacity once his playing days ended. He now takes charge of the whole setup.

The appointment follows Mahela Jayawardene's decision to step down as head coach on October 17, 2026. The change comes at a moment when the franchise is looking to put a disappointing 2026 season behind it.

Pollard played for MI from 2010 to 2022 before moving into the coaching staff ahead of the 2023 season.

"It is an honour to take on the role of Head Coach of Mumbai Indians. MI has been a huge part of my life and career, and the bond I share with this team, the players and the Paltan means a great deal to me" Pollard said.

"I am grateful to Mrs. Nita Ambani, Akash Ambani and the entire MI family for their trust in me. I look forward to working closely with the players and support staff, building on the team's legacy, helping our talent grow and giving the Paltan many more reasons to celebrate."

articles.title: 'Some of the things hurt me': Zimbabwe captain slams players' 'complacency' after series loss as Afghanistan go from 5 for 4 to score 221
articles.summary: Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza was left disappointed with what he called \"complacency\" among some of his teammates after his side suffered a 19-run defeat
articles.body: Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza was left disappointed with what he called "complacency" among some of his teammates after his side suffered a 19-run defeat to Afghanistan in the second T20I in Sharjah on Thursday. The loss also handed Afghanistan an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.Raza said his biggest concern was the attitude of some players after Zimbabwe had reduced Afghanistan to 5 for 4 in the fourth over. He felt the team had taken the opposition lightly at that stage, assuming Afghanistan would struggle to post a big total."For me, before I go too much in detail [about the match] - and I will address that in the changing room - the toughest part to swallow was the complacency that I saw from some of the boys," Raza said after the match.The Zimbabwe captain was particularly unhappy that some players appeared to believe Afghanistan would manage only 130 or 140 runs after losing four wickets early. He said the team needed to stay focused and remember that a match is not over until the final ball."[At 5 for 4] some of the boys were probably calculating that it will be - 130, 140 max - at the end of 20 overs. Some of the things that I saw on the ground today certainly hurt me and I'll address that in the changing room because, listen, it can happen but I think that's where you have to be mentally very strong and say, 'no, the game is never over until it's over - we still have a job in hand and I'm going to be the guy who's going to get the job done'."Before I dissect the game with batting or bowling, I think that's something that I felt today out there in the middle and that's something that needs to be addressed, not to take this game for granted because it can bite back and today is a great example."Zimbabwe had also kept Afghanistan to 45 for 5 at the halfway stage of the innings. However, Azmatullah Omarzai's 116 off 50 balls and Ijaz Ahmad Ahmadzai's 52 off 27 deliveries helped Afghanistan recover and post 221 for 7.Raza then led Zimbabwe's fightback with an unbeaten 106 off 56 balls, but his effort was not enough to prevent defeat. He said he had tried to keep his emotions under control while batting after being unhappy with the team's approach in the first innings."When you're chasing 222, for me the biggest thing was to try and stay in control of my emotions because the way we conducted ourselves in the first innings hurt me," Raza said. "So when we go out to bat, for me it was trying to win the game from any position. That has been our motto and in my head, I was just calculating how best can I go about my business and hopefully the other batters chip in so that we can win the game."Up until the last two overs [by when they needed 46 from 12], we were backing ourselves to win the game but yeah, I think we left ourselves too much."Raza also said he would address the issue with his teammates in the dressing room, making it clear that his message would be stronger than what he had said publicly.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Arshdeep Singh etched his name in the record books during the fourth T20I against New Zealand in Auckland on Friday, becoming the first Indian bowler to
articles.body: Arshdeep Singh etched his name in the record books during the fourth T20I against New Zealand in Auckland on Friday, becoming the first Indian bowler to claim 150 wickets in the shortest format.The left-arm pacer reached the landmark in the final over of his spell when he dismissed New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner for five. Arshdeep bowled a full delivery outside off, forcing Santner to reach for the shot. The batter sliced it towards sweeper cover, where Nitish Kumar Reddy took a well-judged catch near the boundary.Arshdeep finished with his 150th T20I wicket in his 103rd match, further strengthening his position at the top of India's list of leading wicket-takers in the format.He has also reached the milestone in just 1,577 days since making his T20I debut, the quickest by any bowler. He surpassed Sri Lanka's Wanindu Hasaranga, who took 2,325 days to get to 150 wickets.Arshdeep is also among the quickest to the landmark in terms of deliveries bowled. He took 2,143 balls, behind Hasaranga (2,035), Rashid Khan (2,098) and Ehsan Khan (2,143). Among fast bowlers, the previous quickest was Bangladesh's Mustafizur Rahman, who needed 2,532 deliveries.The achievement adds to a remarkable year for Arshdeep. With 40 T20I wickets in 2026, he has become the leading wicket-taker in a calendar year among players from Full Member nations. Ireland's Josh Little took 39 wickets in 2022, while Hasaranga claimed 38 in 2024 and Bhuvneshwar Kumar picked up 37 in 2022.Arshdeep's consistency has also been reflected in his economy rate. articles.title: England vs Australia: Ben Duckett says ODI task 'completely different' to Ashes ahead of November series
articles.summary: Ben Duckett asserts he will bring "confidence'" from hitting two centuries against Pakistan and Sri Lanka in tri-series when England play three ODIs in Australia,, starting in Perth on November 13; Duckett struck career-best 167 during England's win over Sri Lanka in Lahore on Thursday
articles.body:
Duckett arrived in Australia last winter with a reputation as one of the world's best all-format batters, but he averaged 20.2 with a top-score of 42 in 10 innings as England were beaten 4-1.

To compound matters, a video circulated on social media appearing to show Duckett in an inebriated and confused state during England's controversial mid-tour break to the coastal resort town of Noosa.

However, Duckett has an impressive one-day record against Australia, with 470 runs in six matches at 78.33, including hundreds at Bristol in 2024 and Lahore in last year's Champions Trophy.

After recording two more centuries at the Gaddafi Stadium in the last week, Duckett will head to Australia for a three-match ODI series starting on November 13 in Perth in an optimistic mood.

He told the Press Association : "It's a different coloured ball and a different format (from the Ashes).

"I've got two hundreds against Australia in ODIs. It's a completely different format so I'll try to take the confidence from this (tour of Pakistan) into Australia."

Three defeats in a row in Pakistan meant England finished bottom of the tri-series standings but they rounded off their trip by beating Sri Lanka on Thursday, with Duckett making an ODI-best 167.

While he has been off-colour in Tests for the last 12 months, the left-handed opener is one of England's most dependable performers in the 50-over format this year with an average of 56.7.

With Jacob Bethell missing the back end of the English summer and the Pakistan tri-series because of a knee injury, Duckett has struck up an effective opening partnership alongside Tom Banton and the pair have averaged 71 together.

Banton has peeled off five 50-plus scores in six innings, including a maiden hundred for England last month, since his ODI recall to give England a welcome headache with Bethell available to return in Australia.

Duckett added: "Opening with Tom has been great. We obviously haven't done it loads but the small sample we have been together, I feel like it's been working really well.

"It means we've got plenty of guys playing well and to have Jacob coming back in, he's shown what he can do in an England shirt.

"These are good problems to have and problems I'm sure England selectors and coaching staff want."

Hussain: We all know Duckett is high class

Sky Sports Cricket's Nasser Hussain on Ben Duckett:

"We all know that he is a high-class player. He's just had a quiet couple of months and with the cricket they have coming up in this next year it was vitally important that Duckett got his form back."

Former England fast bowler Mark Wood on Ben Duckett:

"If you're having a long career you're going to go through ups and downs.

"Playing innings like that - he obviously loves Lahore, he's got his two best scores there - but they've come at different times and in different competitions so for me his character should be praised here.

"You can see that steel and determination almost when people question him, whether it's about other people maybe coming into the side.

"Whether we've got Bethell, or not, he has stepped up and says: 'no hold on a minute, this is my spot and I'm going to keep that spot for myself'."

articles.body: India spinner Varun Chakaravarthy said head coach Gautam Gambhir has asked the team to aim for a win in every match, even after sealing the five-match T20I series against New Zealand. With India having won the first three games, the spinner said the team was treating the remaining two matches as a separate series and wanted to win both.India entered the fourth T20I at Eden Park in Auckland after winning all three previous matches, with their batters leading the way. So we need to win both the matches,” he said.India's batting had been particularly impressive in the third T20I, when they chased down a target of 199 with 40 balls to spare. Abhishek Sharma led the chase with a 38-ball 113. Chakaravarthy said it would be difficult for the batters to better that performance, but hoped they could produce something similar.“I don't think you can top that, but I hope they can repeat that today. And yeah, they are used to playing in such pitches and such small venues. Yeah, so that played into our advantage for sure,” he said.Chakaravarthy, who is yet to play a match in the series, also spoke about the competition for places in the Indian team. He said players needed to keep working on their game and performing consistently, given the amount of talent available in Indian cricket.“Playing in India, the best thing that you want to happen for yourself is being in the contention. articles.title: James Anderson shocked by Lancashire exit and unsure if he will play elsewhere
articles.summary: Speaking for the first time since his Lancashire exit, James Anderson says the decision made him question whether is "something fundamentally wrong with me as a person".
articles.body:
England legend James Anderson says he is "sad" and "shocked" by his release by Lancashire and has not decided whether to continue his career at another county.

Speaking at length on the Tailenders podcast for the first time since being told he will not have his Lancashire contract renewed, the 44-year-old said the decision made him question whether there is "something fundamentally wrong with me as a person".

Anderson, England's leading wicket-taker and a Lancashire legend, took 50 wickets in the County Championship and served as captain last season but he was told by Lancashire's new hierarchy they want to build an attack for the future.

"I went in for what I thought was a conversation about how the team moves forward," Anderson said.

"It wasn't a great year for the team. Being captain I thought it was chat about that.

"A couple of minutes in I realised it wasn't a conversation. I was being told they thought the best way for the team to move forward was without me.

"I was quite shocked. It was quite brief."

Listen to Anderson on latest Tailenders podcast

Lancashire's decision was made by their incoming director of cricket Paul Farbrace, who held a meeting with Anderson and Lancashire's new chief executive Richard Kenyon.

Despite Anderson's wickets, the club finished second bottom in Division Two of the County Championship.

In 2024, England also chose to move on from their record wicket-taker in similar circumstances as they attempted to refresh and build an attack for the 2025-26 Ashes in Australia.

"All of the way through the season myself and the head coach were like 'is it something we are doing? Could we be doing more to help the team?'" Anderson said.

"I finished the season thinking 'was it something I did? Was I doing something wrong?' - and then I get this news.

"I am thinking 'this is happening again. Is there something fundamentally wrong with me as a person?' Your head just sort of races.

"I wanted to see my career out with Lancs.

"I don't know if my career is done, we will have to wait and see, but it would be nice at some point if someone would let me retire."

'I wouldn't have thought so' - Anderson on Yorkshire move

The decision has angered Lancashire members and was criticised for being "pretty disrespectful" by Anderson's former England bowling partner Stuart Broad, who said it showed a lack of leadership given the veteran was not given a farewell.

Anderson first played List A cricket in 2000 as a 17-year-old for the Lancashire Cricket Board against Suffolk.

In addition to his 911 international wickets - an England record and a record for all pace bowlers - Anderson claimed 443 first-class scalps for Lancashire, along with 83 in List A cricket and a further 50 in T20s.

It is understood other counties are interested in signing the bowler, who turns 45 next summer.

He joked he "wouldn't have thought" he could play for Lancashire's historic rivals Yorkshire, but on his future added: "I am still trying to process everything and weigh up the best way forward for me.

"I am starting to get excited about the future, whether it is something different or playing cricket again. It is exciting.

"There are exciting challenges ahead. I have to attack it like that and not dwell too much on how or why it finished at Lancs."

He added: "I am sad the way it ended with the club I supported as a kid but now I have thought about it I am quite excited for the future.

"I am always going to support Lancashire.

"I was born there, grew up watching them, had some of my most memorable days out with dad watching them, got to play for them and captain the club, which is something most people dream about.

"I feel like I have a special connection with the club and will always support them."
